chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Razi, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man divorces [his wife] while he is absent, let him bear witness to that. So when three pure periods pass from that day, her waiting period has been fulfilled.'
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period calculated for a divorced woman when her husband is absent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that when a husband divorces his wife while absent, the waiting period (iddah) begins from the day the divorce is formally witnessed, ensuring legal certainty for the woman. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on procedural justice and the necessity of witness testimony to validate the start of the iddah, preventing ambiguity in marital status. It underscores the practical application of Quranic principles in personal status law, ensuring the woman's rights are protected even in the husband's absence.
